result.message: Read all 12 supplied evidence files and reviewed the selected operator moe_sum_reduce only. The submitted candidate (.best_kernel.py, identical to best_code in optimize_definition_output.json, subject_sha256 69caad9f... matching ledger round-2 solution) is contract-faithful: it implements exactly solution(input: Tensor[T, top_k, H], routed_scaling_factor: float) -> Tensor[T, H], allocates the output with input.dtype (matching the reference's .to(input.dtype) cast-back), accumulates top-k in float32 like the reference's input.float().sum(dim=1), applies the scalar after the reduction, honors all three input strides and both output strides (including non-contiguous inputs), masks every load/store so the whole returned tensor is written (no uninitialized elements), and reads neither test constants nor the dispatcher. There is no prohibited fallback (no torch.ops, no torch compute for the result), no host synchronization, no environment mutation, and no referenced-but-unimported helper. The num_tokens<=64 / 16x1024 dispatch is a general shape regime, not a case-specific branch, so it is justified specialization rather than benchmark cheating. Measurement evidence is coherent: preflight PASSED with 5 cases and fingerprint f971d2f2..., review_tests evaluate PASSED (reference_source=primary, 8/8 workloads), and the final verification recorded geo_mean 1.3048 (round-2 authoritative 1.2637, ledger best_geo_mean 1.26365) with drift [] and drift_factor 2.0; is_hack is false in every evaluation. The higher retest geo_mean reflects ordinary within-tolerance latency drift (e.g. reference 0.0845 -> 0.0922 ms on workload 00001), not a different candidate. Note that the review_tests attempt is explicitly SKIPPED_EXPLICIT and its subject_sha256 (826c4f86...) is not this candidate hash, so this report does not accept or replace that test-contract review. Only advisory findings are recorded; no P0 conversion/candidate defect was found. Device execution and timing validity remain downstream checks.
